**Comparison**

Both traces follow essentially the same solution path: model the problem as graph 3-coloring, identify the triangles {B,C,H} and {C,D,H}, deduce that B and D must share a color, assign colors to the triangle, propagate to remaining nodes, and verify. Neither trace encounters a dead end or changes strategy.

The key divergence is in post-solution behavior. Trace 1, after finding a valid B=Red coloring, opens one alternative branch (B=Blue) and confirms it works before discarding it, then re-verifies the original solution. Trace 2 is far more exploratory: it opens at least two clear alternative branches (B=Red, E=Blue), confirms each works, discards each, and then re-derives the entire solution from scratch at the end. Neither trace's alternative explorations produce downstream payoff—the solver always returns to the first solution found. The repeated re-derivation at the end of Trace 2 is a clear LOOP with no new information added; Trace 1's re-verification is a milder LOOP of the same kind. No MUSE episodes appear in either trace—all reasoning stays grounded in the graph.

---

**Trace 1 Annotations**

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Now, if B=Blue." end="Let's just stick to the solution I found first:" basis="Opens an alternative branch (B=Blue coloring), works through its implications, confirms it is valid, then explicitly discards it in favor of the original B=Red solution."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's verify the full assignment." end="All valid." basis="Re-executes the same edge-by-edge verification of the same solution that was already performed earlier in the trace, adding no new information."

---

**Trace 2 Annotations**

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's try an alternative just to be sure." end="Both are valid. I'll stick with the first one derived (B=Green) as it was the first thought process." basis="Opens an alternative branch (B=Red coloring), works through all node assignments, confirms validity, then explicitly eliminates it in favor of the original B=Green solution."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's try to make it more balanced?" end="I will stick with the first one I derived (Solution 1). It feels robust." basis="Opens an alternative branch (E=Blue balanced coloring), explores it, confirms it works, then explicitly discards it."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="The problem can be modeled as finding a valid 3-coloring of a graph" end="All pairs have different colors." basis="Re-derives the entire solution from graph construction through triangle identification, color assignment, propagation, and edge-by-edge verification, all of which was already completed earlier in the trace."
